messages:
Samira Patel: Hey finance  quick question. I booked a short-term apartment for a 2-week customer workshop and the vendor charged a $450 refundable security deposit labeled 'SEC DEPOSIT' on the card. Manager approved travel and lodging . Do I submit this now as an expense or wait until it's non-refundable/refunded? Any special category?
Ethan (Finance): Thanks Samira  good Q. Short answer: record it now but mark it as a deposit/pending. We treat refundable deposits differently from regular lodging charges.
Samira Patel: ok thanks  what does 'mark as deposit/pending' look like in Expensify?
Ethan (Finance): In Expensify choose 'Other' -> add note 'Security deposit  refundable' then attach the receipt/authorization. Put the amount and vendor name. In the notes put expected refund date if provided.
Samira Patel: perfect. the vendor email shows this line:
```
Vendor: HarborStay Rentals
Charge: SEC DEPOSIT
Amount: $450.00
Auth ID: 9a3b-REFUND-210
Expected refund window: 7-14 days after checkout
```
Samira Patel: should I cc my manager or anything?
Nate Romero: @Samira Patel I already approved the stay in our travel doc. no need to cc me on the expense, but add a note with the approval link so finance can reconcile.
Ethan (Finance): When the deposit gets refunded, please upload the bank/card refund transaction as a separate expense line with a negative amount and reference the original expense ID. That way our ledger nets to zero.
Samira Patel: neat  do I need to attach the refund screenshot or the bank txn?
Ethan (Finance): Bank txn is best (card statement or online banking screenshot). If refund posts to your card as a credit it will show up automatically in charges. Either way attach proof.
Finance Bot: Reminder: Company policy for refundable deposits  submit initial charge as 'deposit (pending)' and update with refund evidence within 30 days. Failure to reconcile may trigger manual adjustment. See: https://wiki.redwood.com/finance/expense-deposits
Ashley Li: FYI if the deposit becomes non-refundable (e.g., vendor keeps it due to damage or cancellation) we treat it as a lodging expense  just change the category and include manager approval email.
Samira Patel: thanks all. One more  local occupancy tax was charged on top of deposit (line 'Local Tax $35'). Does that stay expensed now?
Ethan (Finance): Yes tax is a real expense even if deposit refunded. Submit tax and fees as separate lines on the same report and mark them as 'lodging taxes/fees'. That part won't get refunded typically.
Samira Patel: Great  I'll submit now with notes and attach vendor authorization + manager approval link. Appreciate the quick help :pray:
Ethan (Finance): Thanks  ping me if you need us to flag the report for manual review. :thumbsup:
